headline: Maui County Council On Aging

meeting.summary: The Council on Aging approved its August 13 minutes, but a motion to approve its plan report stalled without a quorum.
meeting.recap: Eight members were present, enough for a quorum (the minimum needed to hold a meeting).[[0:00:42]] People interviewed by the independent nomination board must wait until March to join the council.[[0:02:55]] The council approved the August 13 minutes by voice vote.[[0:05:34]] A talk on a program that gives breaks to caregivers of people with dementia was moved to the February meeting.[[0:07:11]] The fitness program has about 200 participants and 96 people on a waitlist.[[0:14:32]] Staff plan an instructor training between January and February.[[0:15:59]] Habitat for Humanity has a $250,000 grant to make seniors' homes safer, like adding grab bars.[[0:27:15]] Staff plan a holiday-season campaign warning seniors about scams.[[0:31:40]] The office ordered 15,000 ready-to-eat meals for seniors to use in emergencies.[[0:38:33]] Staff are exploring an on-demand ride pilot using federal emergency funds tied to the wildfires.[[0:44:26]] About 40% of caregivers showed less stress, short of the 80% goal.[[0:45:43]] A motion was made to approve the plan report and let the chair sign it.[[0:51:56]] The next meeting is set for February 11.[[0:55:43]]
decided: The council approved the August 13 minutes by voice vote with no count given.
No vote was taken on the motion because the council no longer had a quorum.
meeting.next: Staff will invite the caregiver program presenter to the February meeting. If there is a quorum at the next meeting, the council can discuss and vote on the report. Staff will receive psychological first aid training from the American Red Cross in 2025.

moments.q: "we finally made it to quorum after about a year of trying"
A member suggests short social media videos aimed at families to warn about scams.
Quorum is lost before the vote on the plan report.
